bull.b: Sustained sequential growth, led by hosting and leasing revenue, indicates expanding monetization of Soluna’s infrastructure beyond proprietary mining. A broader revenue mix can improve business durability by linking results to contracted capacity and customer demand over the next several quarters.

Preserved interconnection capacity is a meaningful infrastructure advantage in a crowded Texas queue. Combined with Soluna’s renewable-powered sites and planned AI capacity, the classification supports continued campus development and strengthens the company’s ability to convert power assets into computing revenue.

A substantially lower debt burden and larger cash balance improve financial flexibility for construction, equipment purchases, and project development. Reduced liens also free project assets and lower balance-sheet pressure, giving Soluna more capacity to pursue its AI infrastructure strategy.

bear.b: Revenue growth is not yet translating into sustainable economics, as near-breakeven gross margin and very large losses consume shareholder capital. Persistently negative operating and free cash flow could require continued external funding and restrict investment in future projects.

Soluna’s planned AI expansion depends on converting preliminary arrangements into binding leases, financing, and completed partnerships. Until those milestones close, the large capacity pipeline may not generate contracted revenue, leaving development spending exposed to execution and customer timing risk.

Losses in both core operating areas show that the current asset base is not consistently producing positive gross economics. Lower mining revenue and weak wind performance reduce internally generated funding, making the transition toward AI hosting more important but also more financially demanding.
